title: Customer submission funnel and risk-scored onboarding matrix
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Build a customer-facing submission funnel and internal triage matrix that automatically scores incoming model/catalog requests using explicit signals (compliance sensitivity, data residency, expected qps, model size, quantization needs, customer SLAs) and inferred signals (usage pattern, likely cost impact, risk of quality regression). The funnel should place requests into lanes (fast-track, standard, security-review, deferred) and recommend an onboarding plan: sandbox, pinned variant, canary rollout, or deprecation timeline. Goal is to reduce manual review time for common requests, improve SLA alignment for enterprise customers, and surface clear eval-gate requirements for high-risk requests.
acceptance_criteria: Public submission form accepts model metadata + enterprise fields (SLA requirement, data residency, regulatory notes, expected throughput)
Automatic scoring system computes a risk score and a cost impact estimate for each submission within 30s
Triage matrix maps score thresholds to lanes with documented actions (e.g., fast-track -> auto-sandbox; high-risk -> security review + custom evals)
Console displays triage result and recommended onboarding path to PMs and Solutions Engineers
At least 3 enterprise pilot customers sign up to use the new funnel and provide feedback
Audit log created for every decision to satisfy Private deployment/compliance needs
implementation_plan: Define schema for submission form fields with Security/Legal and Solutions Engineering input
Prototype a scoring rubric (numeric weights) combining compliance, compute, and quality risk signals
Build serverless intake endpoint + basic UI copy on Console to collect submissions
Integrate scoring service with the internal triage board (Linear view + Console dashboard)
Create actions for each lane: auto-sandbox provision, pin request to staging, schedule security review ticket
Run 2-week pilot with 3 enterprise accounts and adjust thresholds based on false positives/negatives
Ship documentation and run training for Solutions Engineering and CS teams
risks: Scoring rubric may under- or over-index certain signals leading to wrong lane placement
Inaccurate cost estimates could set wrong expectations with customers
Security/legal inputs may change thresholds late in the cycle, requiring rework
Tight coupling with Console UI could delay rollout if design resources are constrained
metrics: Mean time from submission to first triage decision (target < 24 hours for non-high-risk)
% of requests auto-routed without manual PM/SE intervention (target 40% within first quarter)
Pilot customer satisfaction score for intake experience (NPS style)
Accuracy of lane assignment measured by post-triage overrides (target override rate < 15%)
